items.recapEn: At the Yoshiwara bend Fuji switched to the left of the road. Hana listed what she can and cannot do yet: menus and the time, yes; bus signs and swimming, no. Aya, about seven, gave her a paper crane; Hana gave her a Tanabata strip. Ken said the mountain had crossed over, and Hana understood him, more or less.

items.recapEn: At the Left-Fuji stone Ken admitted he could not read the old inscription; Hana could read the character for left, a whole menu and the time. Ken asked for a crane too; Hana cannot fold one yet. Ken said the mountain had gone over to the other side with them, and Hana understood him, more or less.

items.recapEn: Hana wrote home to Yokohama from Yoshiwara: Fuji is on the left of the road here, a girl gave her a paper crane and she gave back a Tanabata strip, she can read menus and tell the time now but still cannot swim, Ken cooks in somebody’s kitchen every day, and tomorrow they plan to walk to Kanbara.
